decision_titles: Traffic barrier preliminary report and funding review
Cooling center report for the City Council
plain_text:
C I T Y   O F   C O N C O R D 
New Hampshire’s Main Street™
141 Green Street • Concord, NH  03301 • (603) 225-8500
 Public Safety Advisory Board
Thursday October 15, 2026 (3:00 PM) – City Council Chambers
DRAFT Meeting Minutes
Members Present: Andrew (Drew) Biemer, Steve Edwards, Councilor and Chair Amanda 
Grady Sexton, Natch Greyes, Councilor Jennifer Kretovic; Kate Lipman, Ana McKenna, 
Councilor Jim Schlosser, Councilor Jeff Foote, Councilor Ali Sekou
City Staff: Interim Police Chief Barrett Moulton, Deputy Police Chief Matt Casey, Deputy 
Police Chief Patrick Ofrias, Police Social Worker Nicole Petrin, and Deputy Fire Chief Mick 
Costello
Guests: Mayor Byron Champlin, Nikki Haas, Project Director, Committee for Concord’s Plan to
End Homelessness.
Minute Taker: Councilor Amanda Grady Sexton and Nicole Petrin
Chair Grady Sexton called the meeting to order at 3:00 P.M.
Approval of Minutes
A motion to approve the minutes from August 20, 2026 was made by Councilor Kretovic and 
seconded by Drew Biemer. The motion passed with no dissenting votes. Councilor Foote 
abstained.
Downtown Safety Issues
Police representatives reported increased foot patrols and directed patrols downtown, including 
outreach by the Community Services Unit and meetings with business owners. Police responded 
to concerns about disruptive behavior, blocked entrances to businesses, camping, and belongings
left on public or private property.
Councilor Kretovic described continuing concerns from businesses about individuals remaining 
outside storefronts, use of customer restrooms by people who are not customers which require 
cleanup demands, and encampments beyond the downtown area. Councilor Foote described 
additional encampments and obstructions along commercial corridors and questioned whether 
expanded services were drawing more people to Concord. Members discussed the need to 
support affected businesses while connecting individuals with assistance.
Chief Moulton described the limits of enforcement and the difficulty of obtaining lasting 
solutions when individuals relocate nearby or repeatedly return to the same property.
C I T Y   O F   C O N C O R D 
New Hampshire’s Main Street™
241 Green Street • Concord, NH  03301 • (603) 225-8500
Police representatives emphasized that enforcement is one part of a broader response and that 
repeated summonses or arrests do not resolve the underlying issues. 
Deputy Chief Casey described recent responses to reports submitted through SeeClickFix
concerning the former Friendly’s property and Kimball Jenkins. Police worked with a property 
owner to clean up the former Friendly’s site and contacted an individual regarding belongings at 
Kimball Jenkins. Staff noted that both locations have required repeated attention.
Members discussed encampments near Integra Drive, including vehicle access to private 
property. Police reported ongoing efforts to communicate with the property owner and noted that
trespass authorization was in place. Possible barriers to vehicle access were discussed, although 
staff noted that barriers would not prevent access on foot. Problem Oriented Policing (POP) 
officers planned to renew their focus on the area after returning from leave and completing work 
at other encampments to include that
Chair Grady Sexton and Ms. Lipman reported a significant decrease in problematic behavior 
near Eagle Square and fewer recent complaints from nearby businesses since the the directed 
patrols began. Councilor Kretovic reported continuing or increased concerns near Storrs Street 
and South Main Street areas. Councilor Sekou asked about activity near Garvins Falls Road. 
Police described directed patrols, resident outreach, and trail checks in response to reports 
involving camping, off highway vehicles, and speeding int hat area. Councilor Foote also 
requested attention to reports of people living at Broken Ground near the previously proposed 
middle school site.
Mr. Biemer noted that staffing and competing calls affect the Police Department’s ability to 
respond to every concern. Councilor Sekou expressed appreciation for the Department’s 
responsiveness.
Police encouraged businesses and residents to call when entrances are blocked or behavior is 
disruptive so that officers can respond and identify patterns. The Chair requested that downtown 
safety remain a recurring agenda item and invited the Chiefs to bring forward any potential 
policy changes for review. Police agreed to provide a more detailed review of activity and 
statistics at the next meeting.
Traffic Barrier Discussion
Deputy Chief Costello reviewed the vehicle barrier system purchased through a Homeland 
Security grant. The system is deployed at certain street events to protect attendees from vehicles 
entering closed areas. Staff explained that deployment, removal, trained personnel, and 
maintaining emergency access require substantial labor at a cost of $1,500 to the City. General 
Services deploys the equipment, and first responser personnel must remain available to open the 
barriers for emergency vehicles.
C I T Y   O F   C O N C O R D 
New Hampshire’s Main Street™
341 Green Street • Concord, NH  03301 • (603) 225-8500
Staff identified Market Days, Halloween Howl, Midnight Merriment, and the annual Holiday 
tree lighting as events for which the City currently designates as “city sponsored events” and 
covers the costs of barriers. The Board was asked to consider which non-sponsored events 
require use of barriers, and how to fund the use of these barriers when a financial hardship is 
demonstrated. Deputy Chief Costello relayed the City Solicitor’s advice that safety 
considerations, rather than an organizer’s ability to pay, should guide deployment requirements.
Members discussed whether all events involving major street closures should require barriers or 
whether the permitting process should rely on an assessment by Police, Fire, and Code 
Enforcement. Members noted that risks include intentional attacks, impaired drivers, and drivers 
who are confused or experiencing another emergency. The appropriate placement of barriers 
may vary for parades, road races, events with a central gathering area, and events extending 
along a route. Members also discussed the need to consider events elsewhere in the City, 
including Loudon Road and Penacook.
Several members supported allowing public safety professionals to determine when barriers are 
required through the existing event review process. Discussion also addressed consistency 
between sponsored and other events, potential municipal liability when barriers are available but 
not used, and the need for guidance from the City Solicitor.
Members considered several approaches to payment, including retaining fees, charging actual 
costs based on the duration and staffing needs of an event, establishing a hardship waiver, or 
having the City absorb costs as part of providing public safety. Councilor Foote requested 
information on the annual number of events and the actual annual cost of deploying barriers. 
Staff estimated approximately 15 major events but agreed that additional information would be 
useful. Councilor Kretovic noted that other City committees were also examining event fees and 
equitable access.
Staff indicated that the remaining major seasonal events discussed were already City sponsored, 
with barrier costs covered, allowing additional time for deliberation. Mr. Greyes made a motion, 
seconded by Mr. Biemer, that 1) Chair Grady Sexton will draft a preliminary report reflecting the
Board’s discussion, including support for public safety staff and Code Enforcement determining 
when barriers are necessary through the permitting process and 2) The PSAB will continue 
reviewing funding options before finalizing its recommendation to the City Council. The motion 
was unanimously approved. The City Solicitor will be invited to the next meeting to address 
liability and related legal questions.
Cooling Center Recommendation
Chair Grady Sexton presented a draft report to the City Council incorporating the Board’s prior 
discussion.
C I T Y   O F   C O N C O R D 
New Hampshire’s Main Street™
441 Green Street • Concord, NH  03301 • (603) 225-8500
Members reviewed the report and identified a correction to a Police and Fire title reference. They
also requested that the statement explaining that the proposal is not a request for City funding be 
bolded. The discussion emphasized a coordinated partnership with willing nonprofit 
organizations.
Mr. Greyes moved to approve the cooling center report for submission to the City Council. 
Councilor Sekou seconded the motion. The motion passed with Mr. Edwards opposed. The Chair
noted that the report would reflect that the recommendation was not unanimous.
Future Agenda Items
Tobacco use referral: The Chair will seek the City Solicitor’s participation to discuss the City’s 
authority to regulate the conduct and businesses addressed in the proposed ordinance. Members 
were asked to review the referral before the next meeting. The Chair will gather background on 
the proposal and approaches under consideration in other municipalities. Members expressed 
interest in addressing underage vaping while clarifying the appropriate legal and enforcement 
approach.
Flock cameras and automated license plate readers referral: Members discussed the Council 
referral and the need to clarify existing State law, permissible camera uses, and pending 
legislation. The Chair will request information from the City Solicitor and the committee will 
review pending state legislative service requests. The matter will be scheduled for December, 
when additional state legislative language may be available. The Board discussed preparing an 
informational report to the Council, which could summarize the legal framework, current 
practices in Concord, and pending legislation.
Drug Enforcement Administration presentation: Chief Moulton reported that a DEA 
representative had agreed to provide an update at the next meeting on drug activity in New 
Hampshire, emerging substances, laboratory testing, and task force work involving Concord. The
presentation is expected to take approximately 30 minutes, depending on questions, and will be 
placed first on the November agenda. Traffic barriers and the tobacco use referral will follow, 
subject to the City Solicitor’s availability.
Adjournment
The Chair thanked members, staff, and guests for their participation and Ms. Haas and Ms. Petrin
for their work on the cooling center proposal. A motion to adjourn was made by Mr. Edwards 
and seconded by Ms. McKenna. The motion passed with no dissenting votes and the meeting 
was adjourned at 4:20 P.M.
